posts.title: 5 Tips for Hair Care This Summer
posts.excerpt: Summer heat and humidity can damage your hair. With these 5 simple tips, keep your mane healthy and shiny all season long.
posts.author: Magnolia Peluquería
posts.content:
# 5 Tips for Hair Care This Summer

Summer in Paraguay can be tough on your hair. Intense sun, humidity, and pool chlorine all work against your mane. But don't worry — here are 5 tips to keep it healthy.

## 1. Deep Condition Weekly
Sun and chlorine dry out hair quickly. Use a deep conditioning mask at least once a week. Ingredients like aloe vera, coconut oil, and keratin help restore lost moisture.

## 2. Sun Protection for Hair
Just like your skin, your hair needs UV protection. Use sprays with SPF or wear a light hat. UV rays fade colored hair and weaken the hair fiber.

## 3. Avoid Hot Water
Hot water opens cuticles and strips natural oils. Rinse with cool or cold water to seal the cuticle and add shine.

## 4. Regular Trims
Summer is perfect for a fresh cut. Schedule a trim every 6-8 weeks to keep split ends at bay.

## 5. Less Heat, More Air-Drying
Reduce flat iron and blow dryer use. Let your hair air-dry whenever possible. Always use a heat protectant if you do use heat tools.

posts.title: How to Choose the Perfect Haircut for Your Face Shape
posts.excerpt: Discover which haircut flatters your face shape: round, oval, square, or heart. Professional tips from Magnolia Hair Salon in Asunción.
posts.author: Magnolia Peluquería
posts.content:
# How to Choose the Perfect Haircut for Your Face Shape

Choosing the ideal haircut isn't just about trends — it's about finding the style that best harmonizes with your face shape. Here's how to find yours.

## Round Face
Go for cuts that create length. Long bob (lob), long layers starting below the jaw, and deep side parts all work well.

## Oval Face
The most versatile shape — almost any cut works. Pixie cuts, long layered hair, and blunt bobs are all great options.

## Square Face
Soften angular jawlines with side-swept layers, soft waves, or a textured long bob.

## Heart Face
Balance a wide forehead with a narrow chin using mid-length layered cuts, side-swept bangs, or bobs with volume at the jawline.

posts.title: Balayage vs. Traditional Highlights: Which Is Better for You?
posts.excerpt: We compare balayage and traditional highlights in technique, maintenance, price, and duration. Discover which coloring technique is ideal for your hair.
posts.author: Magnolia Peluquería
posts.content:
# Balayage vs. Traditional Highlights: Which Is Better for You?

One of the most common questions we get is: balayage or traditional highlights? Both techniques transform your look, but they have key differences.

## Balayage
A freehand technique where color is painted directly onto the hair, creating a natural, sun-kissed gradient from roots to tips. Low maintenance (every 3-4 months), less damage, but more subtle results.

## Traditional Highlights
Uses foils to separate sections of hair for precise, uniform lightening. More defined results, higher contrast, but requires touch-ups every 4-6 weeks.

## Quick Comparison
| Aspect | Balayage | Traditional Highlights |
|--------|----------|----------------------|
| Result | Natural gradient | Defined, uniform |
| Maintenance | Low (every 3-4 months) | High (every 4-6 weeks) |
| Cost | Higher initial | More accessible |
| Damage | Lower | Moderate |

posts.title: Hair Care Routine for Colored Hair
posts.excerpt: Your colored hair deserves special care to keep the color vibrant and the hair fiber healthy. We share the complete routine recommended by Magnolia.
posts.author: Magnolia Peluquería
posts.content:
# Hair Care Routine for Colored Hair

Coloring your hair is an investment in your look, and it deserves special care. Here's the essential routine to keep your color vibrant.

## 1. Use Sulfate-Free Shampoo
Sulfates strip color quickly. Switch to a sulfate-free shampoo formulated for color-treated hair.

## 2. Weekly Hydrating Mask
Colored hair tends to be more porous and dry. A deep conditioning mask once a week is essential.

## 3. Heat Protection
Always use a heat protectant before blow-drying, flat ironing, or curling. It seals the cuticle and prevents color from fading.

## 4. Rinse with Cool Water
Hot water opens cuticles and accelerates color loss. Rinse with cool water to seal the cuticle and lock in color.

## 5. Wash Less Frequently
Each wash removes some pigment. Space washes to 2-3 times per week and use dry shampoo in between.
